speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) what is the cumulative number of applicants for the Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) to date; (b) what are the top three conditions cared for by HCG applicants; and (c) what is the number of applicants broken down by age group of (i) 30 to 39, (ii) 40 to 49, (iii) 50 to 59, (iv) 60 to 69, and (v) 70 years and above.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In an ageing estate, such as Ang Mo Kio, the HCG is very much appreciated.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And while primarily designed for seniors, my understanding is that it is also designed to recognise other forms of caregivers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The first, for those with autism and intellectual disabilities, can the Minister of State clarify whether the individual must also separately meet the Activity of Daily Living (ADL) criteria?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If so, would the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) consider decoupling this?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As the care recipients also have some level of independence and we want to encourage them to maintain these ADLs; the caregivers would greatly appreciate the support.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That is how it is structured, because we see ADLs as being a key function and essential portion of our daily living.
So, HCG itself is a specific scheme for caregivers.
And then, of course, there is the means testing.
I understand and appreciate where the Member is coming from, because there are clearly other concerns with those who are caring for individuals with special needs.
There are many different other schemes that are in place to address many different concerns.
In particular, with regard to those with special needs, there are existing efforts that we are looking at and reviewing, and trying to understand and appreciate better how we can support them.
So, it may not just be from the HCG.
I do see and appreciate the concerns she has with regard to those with other types of caregiving challenges.
And we are looking at some of those to see how we can fill in the gaps.

In the meantime, if there are some specific concerns, she can raise the issues and then, we can see what are the existing infrastructure or support that is already existing that we can channel to the residents who are in need.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, a short supplementary question, please.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I recognise, especially for those with special needs, there may be alternative schemes, for example, through SG Enable.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: However, for the care recipients who are facing mental health conditions, could the Minister of State clarify what sort of testing?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Because for the mental health condition and the doctor issues a total permanent disability, is there an equivalent sort of testing which can be offered to assess ADL, in order for them to qualify for this scheme?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Because my understanding on the ground is that this is a little harder to do; and for mental health conditions, there is not as many schemes available.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I note the Member's concerns that it is not so clear cut.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But there are quite clear descriptions as to what the ADLs are.
